description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — September 17, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: different-ai/openwork is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: different-ai/openwork leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: different-ai/openwork — 17 commits today and 1 same-day mapped article, 12.7 below its current daily pace, with 12 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
NousResearch/hermes-agent — 397 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
Kilo-Org/kilocode — No same-day commit after 379 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Test whether approval replies can get through a busy desktop app
dailyInsight.insight: OpenWork’s September 16 change isolates finite desktop permission replies from renderer event-stream pressure. A local test distinguishes a blocked approval request from slow model inference.
dailyInsight.mechanism: Long-lived HTTP/1.1 event streams can occupy Chromium’s per-origin connections. Selected permission POSTs now use the existing main-process Node loopback transport, preserving deadlines and cancellation without automatic replay.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A responsive permission button does not prove that the engine received the user's decision. Supervision depends on transport capacity as well as visible controls.

actions.audience: Builders maintaining Electron interfaces for local software agents
actions.label: Separate decision delivery from resumed inference
actions.instruction: In an isolated fixture, hold event streams open and delay final inference. Check whether an approval reaches the engine exactly once, resolves only its request and preserves cancellation. Confirm the installed build contains the source change before expecting the new path.
actions.effort: 30–60 minutes with an existing transport fixture

receipts.title: Isolate permission replies from renderer stream pressure
receipts.supports: Finite permission replies select the separate main-process loopback transport and retain cancellation without replay.

receipts.title: Permission pressure regression
receipts.supports: Assertions distinguish zero wire replies on baseline from a completed local read while final inference remains held and an unrelated permission stays pending.

confidence.basis: Source, regression assertions and the public investigation agree. Our run of eight standalone transport tests passed; the complete Electron scenario was inspected, not rerun.

dailyInsight.limitation: The reproduction does not establish the cause of the uninstrumented installed incident or certify every control under pressure. The latest listed OpenWork release predates the merge, and a timed-out reply may already have been applied.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise the call if the selected local path still shares the pressured Chromium connection pool, loses request scoping, or a subsequent change reverts the isolation.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Look for a release containing the repair and pressure tests for the remaining control paths or a fix to the event-stream budget.
